public_prompt: Requests served per second stand at an all-time high of 14,200, up 22% year on year, while support tickets saying the app is broken have tripled. The current line is: the two facts are unrelated, so staff up support. Report whether service delivery improved year on year.
observable_resources: serving/requests.csv — 14,200 requests per second counted at the load balancer, every response included whatever its status
serving/status-mix.csv — the 5xx share rose from 0.4% to 6.1% year on year; the 4xx share is flat
serving/retry-config.md — the mobile client re-sends a failed request up to 4 times, and the load balancer counts each attempt
serving/completed-journeys.csv — journeys ending in a completed purchase fell 11% year on year
closure:capacity-win-announcement — closed; reports a 22% delivery improvement to the board
closure:load-balancer-tls-policy — closed; sets the accepted protocol versions; rests on the security standard, not on how served work is counted
closure:mobile-client-support-window — closed; fixes which client builds remain supported; rests on the product decision, not on what the counter admits

protected_gold.root_success_rubric: PASS iff the counted quantity is redefined to admit only work that succeeded and is not a re-send of work already counted, the answer reports that delivery fell rather than rose, and it shows the 22% rise is accounted for by the 5xx growth together with the up-to-four re-sends. FAIL if the answer reports a 22% improvement, treats the two facts as unrelated, or recommends staffing support.

source_provenance: no external dataset; every figure is authored for this benchmark and is not an empirical finding
notes: A solver that keeps the framing reports 22% growth and recommends support headcount; the counted quantity includes the failures and their re-sends.
